22.0.0.en: God commanded Jeremiah to go down to the king's palace, which lay in a valley surrounded by mountains. This king was Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, the righteous king. Jehoahaz walked in evil and brought idol worship into Jerusalem. God commanded Jeremiah to speak to the king himself so that he might repent, for he had done evil in the sight of the Lord: instead of leading the people to the good, he had turned them away from God. This shows two things:

22.0.1.en: 1- The seriousness of the leader's position, and the importance of using his office to lead the people and not to cause them to stumble.

22.0.2.en: 2- Jeremiah's courage in declaring the truth to the greatest person in the kingdom, bearing the hard consequences if the king became angry with him.

22.1.0.en: At the beginning of his speech, Jeremiah reminds Jehoahaz, king of Judah, that he sits on the throne of David and is of his seed, so he ought to walk as David did in the fear of God and love for Him. He declares that this word is addressed to him, to his servants who help him in governing, and to all the people he rules; that is, he calls the king to obey the word of God and to direct his people to do so after they had drifted away from Him.

22.2.0.en: God calls the king and his helpers to hold fast to justice and righteousness in their judgments: not to side against a person and wrong him because of his weakness, and not to favor the stronger party and so help the oppressor seize the rights of others. He gives examples of the weak, namely strangers, orphans and widows: they are to give them their rights and not oppress them by exploiting their weak circumstances. Injustice may even reach the point of killing an innocent person, or at least of stripping him of his rights and pressing him down, as though they had killed him and shed his blood; that is, they took away his right to live and crushed him by their wrongdoing.

22.2.1.en: Be just in your judgments. Do not be swayed by the position or power of some, so that you deny the wronged his rights and let the wicked and powerful rob him. If you have authority, strive to stop the evil; and if you cannot, at least help the wronged with all your strength.

22.3.0.en: God promises them as a reward, if they follow justice in their judgments, that the throne of their kingdom will be established, and that strong kings from their offspring will enter this palace to sit on the throne, possessing great chariots and horses, and strong servants and people.

22.4.0.en: On the other hand, He threatens them that if they do not obey His word and persist in their injustice and in encouraging the unjust, He will lay waste this royal palace, and even what is more important, His own house and temple. The people of the kingdom of Judah and their kings thought that God would protect them because the temple of God was in their city, Jerusalem, and that this temple would remain until the end of days because they were the offspring of David. They forgot that they must walk as David did and offer pure worship in the temple of God in order to enjoy His protection.

22.5.0.en: Gilead: a fertile region full of high mountains.

22.5.1.en: The head of Lebanon: one of the high, fertile mountains of Lebanon.

22.5.2.en: He likens the king's palace, which relies on its strength, to the lofty mountains of Gilead or Lebanon, full of fertility and relying on their greatness, strength and firmness: even so, it will be shattered and laid waste because it disobeyed God. He says "cities" and not "a city" because the whole kingdom of Judah will be shattered because of its evils, and not Jerusalem alone.

22.6.0.en: God declares that He will appoint and consecrate Babylon to destroy the cities of Judah. The Babylonians were distinguished by felling timber, so they attacked the house of God, the king's palace and the palaces of the great with their axes, to break up their timbers taken from cedar trees and burn them with fire. The Babylonians thought that their god was stronger than the God of Israel, and God tolerated this in order to discipline His people so that they would repent; afterward He would discipline Babylon by the kingdom of the Medes and Persians, who would shatter it.

22.7.0.en: After the destruction of Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, travelers will pass by these ruins and marvel at their devastation, because they had been very great. Each one will ask his neighbor why they were destroyed, and he will answer him: because of their disobedience to God, their breaking of the covenant with Him, and their turning to worship foreign, pagan gods.

22.8.0.en: Bewail him: they utter words of lament over him after his death.

22.8.1.en: The dead man mentioned is Josiah the king, who died in the battle of Megiddo in 609 BC at the age of 38. He was a righteous king, and therefore the people who loved him wept for him when his chariot was brought back to his land, and they buried him with great honor.

22.8.2.en: But Jeremiah calls the people to weep for his son, the new king Jehoahaz, whom Necho king of Egypt would seize and carry captive to Egypt, where he would die and never return to his land. The last king of Assyria had become very weak and the armies of the Babylonians had begun to grow strong against him, so the king of Egypt went out with his armies to support him. He took possession of Palestine, seized Jehoahaz and sent him to Egypt.

22.9.0.en: He calls Jehoahaz by his former name, "Shallum," because he was not Josiah's firstborn but the fourth of his sons, and he seized the kingdom by force. He sat on the throne only three months and ten days; the king of Egypt seized him and sent him there, where he died and never returned to his land. So he calls him by his former name because he was a usurper of the kingdom, and he was wicked and not righteous like his father; this evil came upon him in his captivity to Egypt.

22.10.0.en: Jehoahaz died in Egypt and never returned to his land; that is, he died in exile because of his evil.

22.10.1.en: Do not rejoice in seizing the rights of others who cannot resist you, for God, who is able to do all things, sees you and will punish you if you do not repent. So remember always that you stand before God, and fear Him in all your works, words and thoughts, and live in purity, so that you may enjoy His care and love.

22.11.s.en: (3) Pride and love of material things

22.11.0.en: Chambers: upper rooms in the house.

22.11.1.en: Jeremiah addresses his words to King Jehoiakim, whom Necho king of Egypt made king over the kingdom of Judah after Jehoahaz his brother was carried captive to Egypt. Sadly, Jehoiakim did not learn or benefit from what happened to his brother by returning to God in repentance. Instead he was concerned to build himself a house, that is, a great palace of several stories. For this he used his poor people, who were pressed by the heavy taxes the king collected to pay tribute to the king of Egypt and to enjoy the pleasures of life himself. The word "neighbor" means the Jewish people: he wronged his people and exploited them in building without wages. He was unjust and unfair in order to satisfy his pride and his love of material things, which appeared in the building of the great palace, built with the money of injustice which he took from the people.

22.12.1.en: Ceiled: he makes the roof of the palace.

22.12.3.en: He describes the details of the great palace which Jehoiakim took care to make spacious, with its roof of the most precious timber, the wood of cedar trees. He also took care to paint it with materials containing glue so that they would stick to the walls; that is, he took care to erect a palace of the highest standard to satisfy his lust and his pride.

22.13.0.en: Closest to: on a level with.

22.13.1.en: Jeremiah rebukes him for his pride, which he compares to his rising high to be on a level with the tall cedar trees. He calls him to humility, following the example of his father Josiah, who was content with necessary food and drink and not with a palace and luxurious foods; so God blessed him and he lived in much prosperity.

22.14.0.en: He praises King Josiah, the father of Jehoiakim, calling his son to imitate him, for Josiah took care to provide for the poor, not to wrong them, and to give them their rights, as well as every needy and destitute person; by this he demonstrated his knowledge and fear of God.

22.15.0.en: He rebukes Jehoiakim for the shocking injustice into which he had fallen: he snatched the rights of others and exploited the poor in building his palace, exhausting their strength until they fell dead from weariness and overwork.

22.16.1.en: Because of Jehoiakim's great injustice to his people, they hated him. So when the king of Babylon attacked Jerusalem and killed Jehoiakim, no one grieved for him; they did not weep for him or lament him; the people did not say to one another, "Ah, my brother!" or "Ah, my sister!" and ask why this had happened; nor did they cry out in sorrow that they had lost their lord and their great man, but they made light of his death. When Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon killed him, he threw him outside the city without burial, and they dragged his body as the carcass of a dead donkey is dragged, and buried him without any honor. This was the result of his injustice to his people and his using the money of his subjects to build his palace and satisfy his pleasures.

22.16.2.en: Do good to all those around you as far as you are able, even to those who wrong you and treat you unjustly and do not thank you for your kindnesses. Be sure that all your works are precious to God. And after you depart from this life, those who wronged you may be moved and return to God, because deep within they cannot deny your love.

22.17.0.en: Bashan: lies to the northeast of Jerusalem.

22.17.1.en: Abarim: lies to the southeast of Jerusalem.

22.17.2.en: Jeremiah calls on rebellious Jerusalem, persisting in her sins, to go up on the mountains in the regions surrounding her, namely Lebanon, which lies to her north, and likewise Bashan and Abarim, to weep over the evil that will come upon her, just as the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite went up to weep over herself before she died (Judg 11:37, 38). Jerusalem is to weep not only over her coming destruction, but also over the surrounding countries that allied themselves with her, such as Egypt, because it fell into the hand of Babylon, who shattered it; for Babylon overcame Egypt in the battle of Carchemish in 605 BC (Jer 46:2-12). That is, no one was found to help Jerusalem in her affliction; she was destroyed together with all her lovers because she had rebelled against the Lord.

22.18.0.en: God punishes Jerusalem because He called her to repentance at a time when she was at rest from the wars of her enemies, but she refused to listen to Him and repent. This has been her nature for many years, so she persists in disobedience even when the time of her ruin draws near, and she refuses God's warnings to her.

22.18.1.en: Do not accept any sin, even a small one such as a thought or an evil word, lest you become accustomed to it and it leads you to greater evils that destroy your life, as you do not benefit from God's warnings because of your negligence. He loves you, so why do you neglect His voice and despise His love?...!

22.19.0.en: The wind shall feed them: they lose all shepherding, and the wind scatters them.

22.19.1.en: By "your pastors" is meant your kings, O Jerusalem, and your rulers, who will lose all care and protection because they forsook God.

22.19.2.en: By the shepherds is also meant the kings of the countries surrounding Jerusalem, who will lose their strength before the king of Babylon and so be unable to support Jerusalem. Then she will be put to shame when Babylon attacks and destroys her, and there will be no one to rescue her, because the countries around her will themselves have been carried captive to Babylon.

22.20.0.en: God addresses Jerusalem, which dwells on the mountain like the mountains of Lebanon, which built palaces within her of the wood of the strong cedars of Lebanon, and felt secure within them, declaring that she will be destroyed by the hands of Babylon and her pains will be very severe, like the pains of a woman who travails at childbirth, and all who are around her will pity her.

22.21.0.en: After Nebuchadnezzar killed King Jehoiakim, his son Jehoiachin, who is also called Coniah, reigned. He reigned for three months and walked in evil like his father (2 Kgs 24:8-17). Nebuchadnezzar seized him and carried him captive to Babylon, where he died.

22.21.1.en: Here God swears by Himself, to confirm His word, declaring that however great Coniah may be as king, God will pluck him from his kingdom and carry him captive to Babylon, even if he were firm and great like a signet on the right hand of God, that is, in perfect strength, for the right hand signifies strength.

22.22.0.en: God warns Jehoiachin through the mouth of Jeremiah, that perhaps he may repent and turn back from his evil. He tells him that He will deliver him into the hand of the king of Babylon, Nebuchadnezzar (Nebuchadrezzar), the strong and dominant king of whom Jehoiachin was afraid, who will carry him captive to the land of the Chaldeans, that is, Babylon.

22.23.0.en: He also warns him that he will be carried captive to a foreign land in which he was not born, namely Babylon, he and his mother, who is called Nehushta (2 Kgs 24:8, 15), and they will not return to their homeland but will die in captivity, as a symbol of the eternal destruction that awaits the wicked.

22.24.0.en: Jehoiachin and his mother longed to return from Babylon to Jerusalem, but they did not return because of their evil. This shows that the whole family lived in evil: King Jehoiakim, his wife Nehushta, and their son Jehoiachin, the young man of eighteen years (2 Kgs 24:8-9).

22.25.0.en: A vessel wherein is no pleasure: God takes no pleasure in it.

22.25.1.en: God looks with sorrow and fatherly love at King Jehoiachin (Coniah), how he was carried captive to Babylon and cast down there in humiliation, as a broken earthen vessel of no use is cast away. The great man became lowly, and all this because of sin. So the wrath of God came upon him and his offspring.

22.26.0.en: God calls the earth to witness against Jehoiachin's evil and his humiliating end as a punishment for him. He says that although Jehoiachin has offspring, none of them will reign after their father or recover their father's throne, and so he is considered "childless" in that none of his sons will reign. Thus the reign of the descendants of David over the kingdom of Judah comes to an end; but in the fullness of time Christ, the Son of David, comes to reign over the hearts of those who believe in Him, not only from among the Jews but from the whole world.

22.26.1.en: Consider the consequences of your sins, which lead to destruction and separate you from God, so that you hasten to repent of them. Then you will gain the salvation of your soul and rejoice the heart of God.

22.26.2.en: Christ the Savior and the false prophets

23.0.0.en: God warns the rulers, the priests and all those responsible for His people in the kingdom of Judah, because instead of gathering God's people they scattered them and drove them away from Him; indeed they led them astray and destroyed them by spreading idol worship among them and encouraging them in evil. This was at the end of the kingdom of Judah in the days of King Zedekiah, when Babylon began to attack Jerusalem and the kingdom of Judah.

23.1.0.en: God threatens these wicked shepherds that He will punish them for their walking in evil, their failure in shepherding, and their leading His people astray.

23.2.1.en: God Himself intervenes to gather His people who walked in evil. God disciplines them with captivity and dispersion in the kingdom of Babylon, then brings them from the land of Babylon and restores them from captivity to Jerusalem and Judea, and blesses them so that they increase and multiply.

23.3.0.en: God promises to raise up shepherds who will care for His flock. These are His righteous men who brought them back from captivity, Zerubbabel, Ezra and Nehemiah, and He also means the Apostles of the New Testament and the bishops and priests in the Church. Thus the flock is reassured and the devil cannot snatch it away.

23.4.0.en: Here he speaks clearly about the awaited Messiah, the true Shepherd of the people of God. He likens Him to a Branch because He is joined to the root, that is, the "tree of David," being of his seed, and because He became incarnate in order to grow in our midst and complete our righteousness by our redemption on the Cross. Christ shepherds His people successfully and rules with truth and justice.

23.5.0.en: Here he speaks of Christ the Savior, who saves His people by His death on the Cross, and so saves the two kingdoms of the Jews, Judah and Israel, and even the whole world of those who believe in Him. God justifies His children by taking their sins away from them and granting them His virtues, so that we become righteous by the grace of God; that is, Christ becomes the cause of our righteousness.

23.6.0.en: He prophesies about the return from captivity, that is, from Babylon to Jerusalem, which will be a very great and unexpected event, its report rising above the report of the exodus from Egypt and its bondage. All this is a symbol of liberation from sin by the redemption of Christ, and then of liberation from the burden of the body and the passing world by entering the Kingdom of Heaven.

23.6.1.en: If you find no one to listen to you or guide you, and you find a shortcoming in the spiritual care offered to you, do not be troubled. Be sure that God is able to shepherd and guide you by different means, so that you are saved and find your place in heaven.

23.7.0.en: Jeremiah looked at the evil of the false prophets, which deserved God's wrath against them. Before he utters the words of God for their punishment, his fatherly love for them appears in the breaking of his heart for them, that is, the anguish of his feelings over what would come upon them, and likewise the shaking of his bones, that is, the weakness of his body in its strongest part, the bones. Indeed, from grief over their evil end he came to stagger like a man drunk with wine.

23.7.1.en: Be compassionate toward sinners even while you call them to repentance. Your tenderness wraps around your rebuke of them, and as they feel your fatherly love their hearts are moved to return to God. God looks upon your prayers for them, forgives them, and leads them to the way of the new life with Him.

23.8.0.en: Adulterers: the disobedient who walk in uncleanness.

23.8.1.en: Through the prophecies of the false prophets, evil, idol worship, adultery and every uncleanness spread in Jerusalem and around it. So the curse of God came upon them and the land lost its fertility and its pastures; that is, neither man nor beast found food, and man's effort turned to worshiping idols and doing uncleanness with all his strength.

23.9.0.en: The prophets and priests also shared with the people in these evils, so much so that they set up images of foreign gods in the house of the Lord and engraved them on its walls.

23.10.0.en: God punishes them, since the way of their adultery made them slide from evil to evil, like one who slips on a slope in the dark, stumbles and cannot rise. God allows them to be driven out of their land at the hand of Babylon and to fall slain by the sword, and He punishes them in the year of Babylon's attack on them, in which they destroy Jerusalem and burn it.

23.10.2.en: 13- And I have seen folly in the prophets of Samaria; they prophesied in Baal, and caused my people Israel to err. 14- I have seen also in the prophets of Jerusalem an horrible thing: they commit adultery, and walk in lies: they strengthen also the hands of evildoers, that none doth return from his wickedness: they are all of them unto me as Sodom, and the inhabitants thereof as Gomorrah. 15- Therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts concerning the prophets; Behold, I will feed them with wormwood, and make them drink the water of gall: for from the prophets of Jerusalem is profaneness gone forth into all the land. 16- Thus saith the LORD of hosts, Hearken not unto the words of the prophets that prophesy unto you: they make you vain: they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the LORD. 17- They say still unto them that despise me, The LORD hath said, Ye shall have peace; and they say unto every one that walketh after the imagination of his own heart, No evil shall come upon you. 18- For who hath stood in the counsel of the LORD, and hath perceived and heard his word? who hath marked his word, and heard it? 19- Behold, a whirlwind of the LORD is gone forth in fury, even a grievous whirlwind: it shall fall grievously upon the head of the wicked. 20- The anger of the LORD shall not return, until he have executed, and till he have performed the thoughts of his heart: in the latter days ye shall consider it perfectly. 21- I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran: I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied. 22- But if they had stood in my counsel, and had caused my people to hear my words, then they should have turned them from their evil way, and from the evil of their doings.

23.11.0.en: The false prophets walked in lying to please the kings, and by their prophecies they helped spread the worship of Baal in the northern kingdom, the kingdom of Israel, whose capital was Samaria. All this led the people astray and drew them away from God.

23.12.0.en: The false prophets in Jerusalem also shared in lying, and led the people of God astray like the prophets of Samaria. They walked in disobedience and uncleanness, and even encouraged the wicked instead of rebuking them. So they became brothers of Sodom and Gomorrah; that is, their evil increased greatly and they deserved destruction like Sodom and Gomorrah.

23.13.1.en: The water of gall: very bitter water.

23.13.2.en: God expresses His punishment and discipline of the false prophets by making bitter wormwood their food and the water of gall their drink, that perhaps they may repent, especially since the lying of the prophets of Jerusalem spread to the neighboring lands and led everyone astray.

23.14.0.en: The false prophets persist in their lying and attribute their words to God, while God is utterly innocent of them. Therefore God speaks with power, declaring His title the Lord of hosts, that is, the Mighty One, and commands His people not to listen to the false prophets, because what they say is vain and useless: it is what they themselves see, and not God.

23.15.0.en: Sadly, the false prophets encourage the wicked to persist in evil, so that they despise God, worship idols and stubbornly insist on sin; yet the false prophets promise them peace, security and blessings.

23.16.0.en: Jeremiah asks whether there is a single one of these prophets who has stood in the council of God with His saints, or whether all of them lie and claim to have heard from God.

23.17.2.en: Since the prophets persisted in their lying, God was angry with them and threatened them with discipline like the blowing of a whirlwind and a violent wind upon them and upon their heads, to trouble and destroy them.

23.18.0.en: The latter days: the end of their opportunity for repentance, when His wrath rises against them, as happened in the Babylonian attack and the captivity. God declares that His wrath will continue to destroy the disobedient until God makes manifest the punishment of sin and everyone who is ready to repent repents.

23.19.0.en: God repeats that He is innocent of all that the false prophets said.

23.20.0.en: God affirms that these prophets are liars, for if they were true prophets they would have stood in the council of God through their prayers and holiness, and they would have heard the voice of God and spoken His words.

23.20.1.en: Do not teach others anything you have not heard in the Church, lest your teaching be false and cause others to stumble and drive them away from God. Be humble and be a disciple in the Church, and declare your lack of knowledge if you do not know, so that you may ask and learn the sound teaching.

23.20.2.en: (4) Dreams and the claim to prophecy (vv. 23-40)

23.20.3.en: 23- Am I a God at hand, saith the LORD, and not a God afar off? 24- Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? saith the LORD. Do not I fill heaven and earth? saith the LORD. 25- I have heard what the prophets said, that prophesy lies in my name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed. 26- How long shall this be in the heart of the prophets that prophesy lies? yea, they are prophets of the deceit of their own heart; 27- Which think to cause my people to forget my name by their dreams which they tell every man to his neighbour, as their fathers have forgotten my name for Baal. 28- The prophet that hath a dream, let him tell a dream; and he that hath my word, let him speak my word faithfully. What is the chaff to the wheat? saith the LORD. 29- Is not my word like as a fire? saith the LORD; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces? 30- Therefore, behold, I am against the prophets, saith the LORD, that steal my words every one from his neighbour. 31- Behold, I am against the prophets, saith the LORD, that use their tongues, and say, He saith. 32- Behold, I am against them that prophesy false dreams, saith the LORD, and do tell them, and cause my people to err by their lies, and by their lightness; yet I sent them not, nor commanded them: therefore they shall not profit this people at all, saith the LORD. 33- And when this people, or the prophet, or a priest, shall ask thee, saying, What is the burden of the LORD? thou shalt then say unto them, What burden? I will even forsake you, saith the LORD. 34- And as for the prophet, and the priest, and the people, that shall say, The burden of the LORD, I will even punish that man and his house. 35- Thus shall ye say every one to his neighbour, and every one to his brother, What hath the LORD answered? and, What hath the LORD spoken? 36- And the burden of the LORD shall ye mention no more: for every man's word shall be his burden; for ye have perverted the words of the living God, of the LORD of hosts our God. 37- Thus shalt thou say to the prophet, What hath the LORD answered thee? and, What hath the LORD spoken?

23.20.4.en: 38- But since ye say, The burden of the LORD; therefore thus saith the LORD; Because ye say this word, The burden of the LORD, and I have sent unto you, saying, Ye shall not say, The burden of the LORD; 39- Therefore, behold, I, even I, will utterly forget you, and I will forsake you, and the city that I gave you and your fathers, and cast you out of my presence: 40- And I will bring an everlasting reproach upon you, and a perpetual shame, which shall not be forgotten.

23.21.0.en: God asks in astonishment: Am I like the limited pagan gods who exist in a particular place?! Of course not. Am I a God at hand, and not present in distant places?! God answers that He is present everywhere, so He sees everything that is hidden and concealed, and He fills heaven and earth.

23.22.0.en: God declares His displeasure with the false prophets who claim to have seen dreams and relate them to people as divine revelations.

23.23.0.en: God declares that these prophets are liars and deceivers.

23.24.0.en: God rebukes these prophets: their false dreams and their claim to prophecy draw them away from God and bind them to idol worship such as Baal, and this is a grave sin because it leads the people astray from God.

23.25.0.en: God asks the true prophet, to whom God reveals a vision, to speak it, like the prophet Jeremiah; as for the liars, let them fall. God marvels at the existence of the false prophets, whom He likens to chaff, alongside the true prophet Jeremiah, whom He likens to wheat.

23.26.0.en: Then God continues, declaring that His word is like the fire that consumes chaff, that is, it exposes the deceit of the false prophets who are likened to chaff, and thus God exposed these false prophets. God also likens His word to a hammer that breaks the stony hearts of these prophets.

23.27.0.en: These prophets also fell into the sin of stealing, for they heard the prophets of God such as Jeremiah or Baruch, took their words, and claimed that God had guided them to them by dreams and visions, adding their own thoughts to them.

23.28.0.en: God declares His war on the false prophets who claim private thoughts, uttering them with their tongues and saying that God is the one who said them; they falsely ascribe themselves to God.

23.29.0.en: God affirms that He is against the false prophets who boast of their claims and their false dreams; they did not profit my people in anything, but led them astray.

23.29.1.en: Do not ascribe the thoughts of others to yourself in order to find greater honor, lest you bring upon yourself the wrath of God because of your pride and your lying. Be humble, and God will grant you great and deep knowledge.

23.30.0.en: When the people, or the prophets, or the priests ask Jeremiah about the burden of the Lord, he is to say that the Lord has declared it and that He rejects them because of their evils.

23.31.0.en: God repeats that He will punish everyone who claims prophecy and knowledge of the burden of the Lord, whether among the false prophets, the priests, or any individual of the people.

23.32.0.en: He requires the people to seek out the word of God which His true prophets declare, such as Jeremiah or Baruch, and no longer to claim knowledge of the burden of the Lord.

23.33.0.en: God reproaches them in sorrow, saying that what they speak is their own burden and their own thoughts, and not the burden of the Lord and His word.

23.34.0.en: God mocks the claims of the false prophets, and requires Jeremiah to confront them and say to this deceiving prophet, "What has God said to you?", that perhaps he may take heed and repent of his deceit and lying.

23.35.0.en: God ends His speech by threatening the false prophets who persist in claiming prophecy that He will punish them by forgetting them, that is, abandoning them and their city Jerusalem. The Babylonians will attack it, destroy it and burn it, and the city of the fathers, Jerusalem, in which is the temple of God, will become a reproach and a shame before all peoples because of the evil and disobedience of the people of God.
